title: Rav Acha, Governor of the Fortress
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived in Rav Ami’s time, as in [Yevamot 45a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45a.4): he and R' Tanchum son of R' Chiyya of Kefar Akko redeemed captive women who came from Armon to Tiberias — and they came before R' Ami, etc. In [Ketubot 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.88a.9) he relates an incident that came before R' Yitzchak [Nappacha — so it is in [Arakhin 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.22b.9)] in Antioch, and [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Ketubot.88a.9.1) explains that “Governor of the fortress” was Acha’s epithet. He is mentioned in [Ketubot 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.22a.10) and [Bava Batra 146a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.146a.7), where they said, “And this halakhah Rav Acha, governor of the fortress, brought up before the sages at Usha”; in Hyman’s plain-sense interpretation this does not belong to the baraita, and likewise, he writes, “we find” in [Ketubot 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.50a.11) that Rabbi Abbahu and Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef also were at Usha. [Yuchasin](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=13) wrote, “There is also a Rav Acha, governor of the fortress, in chapter 2 of the Tosefta,” and forgot to note in which tractate; Hyman adds, “I have not found it anywhere in the Tosefta.” If it is indeed found so, Hyman concludes that “we are compelled to say” that there were two named Rav Acha, governor of the fortress, and the Rav Acha who brought [the halakhah] up before the sages at Usha was a Tanna, because [Rashbam on Bava Batra 146a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Bava_Batra.146a.7.1) places the episode when the Sanhedrin sat there. Hyman leaves the question open.[^4]

The London 1857 Yuchasin (p. 109) gives chapter 2 of the Tosefta and leaves the tractate unnamed. The Tosefta passage remains unidentified. Yevamot 45a names Tanchum son of Chiyya of Kefar Akko as Acha’s companion when they come before Ami. The preceding line in that Yuchasin printing gives Pinchas son of Chiyya for the encounter before Ami. Ketubot 88a gives Yitzchak in Antioch, and Arakhin 22b gives Yitzchak Nappacha. Rashi calls ‘Governor of the fortress’ his epithet. Ketubot 22a and Bava Batra 146a ascribe rulings at Usha to Acha. Rashbam places the latter ruling when the Sanhedrin sat there, and Ketubot 50a names Abbahu and Yitzchak bar Yosef at Usha in a separate episode. The distinction between two figures remains Hyman’s conditional proposal.

The [London 1857 Yuchasin, p. 109](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=13) cites chapter 2 of the Tosefta without naming a tractate. Its preceding line names Pinchas son of Chiyya, where [Yevamot 45a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45a.4) names Tanchum. [Seder HaDorot 298](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=298&lang=en) also notes this difference and raises a chronological question about Usha. The Tosefta passage remains unidentified.
